b:
One day in a dream, someone
sprinkled me with a spray of imagination

The sky was in our grasp;
we rose up proud as a comet,
travelled even beyond the Milky Way,
and there too
we shouted the essence of reason

Levelling every hill and hollow,
the people who filled the earth stood rejoicing;
blowing conch shells, they celebrated
that caste was finally gone

On Buddha Purnima
we sang Purandara Dasa's hymns,
and on the festival of giving
we remembered the sacrifices of Jesus

Hunger was not ours; among us
there was no such word as starvation.
We did not eat for taste;
we said a strong body was the truth

Women walking the town at midnight;
here not even dogs are needed to guard them.
Calling her mother, calling her sister,
true manhood here worships her

A child gives a loving kiss,
and hearing her say
"there will be no more Asifas,"
great bliss is born here

Call it a dream, call it fancy,
if you see it through to the end, it becomes real;
like a pearl this land will flourish
for certain, one day. This is the truth

Until then,
with dreams,
I,
we
note: Purandara Dasa was a Carnatic saint-composer. "The festival of giving" (Eekai Thirunaal) is Eid ul-Fitr, so each line mixes festivals of different faiths on purpose. "No more Asifas" refers to Asifa Bano, an eight-year-old girl raped and murdered in Kathua, India, in 2018.
